title: Caffeine-Timing vs Sleep-Quality Correlation
dataSources: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body composition (`bodycomp:measure`).
app: Biohacking and advanced-health data — HRV chest straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=espresso:shot OR sourcetype=oura:daily)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(strftime(_time,"%H")>=14,caffeine_mg,0))) as late_caffeine, avg(sleep_score) as sleep by _time
| eval high_late=if(late_caffeine>100,1,0)
| stats avg(sleep) as avg_sleep by high_late
description: Compares your sleep quality on days with and without late-afternoon caffeine, testing the advice on your own body.
value: Generic caffeine advice may not fit you; comparing your own late-caffeine days to the rest gives a personal, convincing answer.
implementation: Ingest caffeine timing and sleep scores into `index=personal`; compare average sleep by whether you had late caffeine.
visualization: Bar chart of average sleep score with versus without late caffeine.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how well you sleep on days you had afternoon coffee versus days you did not, testing the advice on you.
